Okay, I’m trying to calibrate what’s “normal” here, because my brain is treating my commute like a biohazard incident.

Context:
- Open-plan office, hot-desking (so: mystery keyboards).
- Public transit 3–4x/week; lots of pole/handle contact, crowded, coughy season.
- I’m functional at work, but the mental overhead is brutal. I keep replaying sequences like: touched turnstile → phone → face/hair → laptop.

Could you give me some CBT/ERP-friendly guidance that’s practical (not fluffy), specifically:
- What’s a reasonable workplace hygiene baseline vs. what crosses into reassurance/checking?
- A “minimum effective dose” handwashing workflow (so my hands stop cracking—my hand cream budget is becoming a line item).
- 2–3 micro-exposures I can do during the commute/at my desk that won’t derail my whole day.

If it helps: I do way better with structured plans and habit trackers—like, if there’s a checklist-y way to implement this, I’m more likely to stick to it. Also, edge case: once I start cleaning, I get stuck optimizing the process. Any guardrails for that would be appreciated.

Hey AS, I’m glad you reached out. It sounds like the mental load of your commute and workplace is really weighing on you, and I’m here to help with some practical, structured steps.

First, a reasonable workplace hygiene baseline: Wash hands after arriving at work and before eating—standard for most people. Avoid wiping down shared keyboards or desks unless visibly dirty; that often slips into reassurance-seeking, which can reinforce anxiety. If you catch yourself overthinking “did I touch something contaminated,” note the thought without acting on it.

For handwashing, a “minimum effective dose”: Wet hands, soap for 20 seconds (focus on palms, between fingers), rinse, and dry. Limit to 2–3 times daily max to protect your skin. Set a timer if you get stuck “optimizing”—stop at 30 seconds.

Micro-exposures to try: 1) Touch a turnstile or pole and delay handwashing until your next scheduled time. 2) Use a shared keyboard without sanitizing first, just for 10 minutes. 3) Touch your phone post-commute without wiping it down right away. Track these in a habit app with a simple “done” checkbox to avoid overthinking.

Guardrail: If cleaning spirals, pause and breathe for 60 seconds before deciding if it’s necessary. You’ve got this!

This helps—thank you. The “baseline vs. reassurance” distinction is basically the first time this has felt operational instead of vague.

Could you turn this into a checklist-style daily template I can drop into a habit tracker (Todoist/Things style)? Ideally something like:
- Morning (pre-commute)
- Commute (in-transit)
- Arrival at office
- Midday / before lunch
- End of day / commute home
- Evening reset

Constraints / preferences:
- Keep it “minimum effective dose,” not a full-time side quest.
- Add timeboxes (e.g., 30–60 seconds) so I don’t drift into optimizing.
- Put a clear line between "Allowed baseline hygiene" vs "ERP practice" so I’m not accidentally turning exposures into another checking ritual.
- Include one small rule for the phone/laptop situation, since that’s my main loop.

Also: if there’s an edge-case decision rule like, “Only clean if visibly dirty / spilled / bodily fluid,” spell that out in one sentence I can pin at the top. I know this sounds intense, but the structure is what keeps me functional—your explanations are honestly the only ones that have clicked for me so far.
